clue.text: Youth given unknown sentence — one with spots

parts.note: a youth is a lad
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
bird (from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' = time) is British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A young man is handed a prison term and comes out covered in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD meaning time in prison is British slang, from the rhyming slang bird-lime for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the small beetle by its familiar spotted wing cases, a cryptic description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Cough mixture supplied by trade union in Grimsby area?

indicators.note: in places the union's abbreviation within the county's abbreviation

parts.note: Grimsby is a port in Lincolnshire, abbreviated Lincs

explanation.surface: Cough syrup provided by a workers' union around Grimsby.
explanation.definitionFit: A syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough or sore throat.

clue.text: Strained, having produced sketch

definitions.meaning: a strained, haggard face looks tired and tense
past participle of the verb for making a sketch

explanation.definitionFit: One word meaning both haggard and tense in the face, and sketched with pencil.

clue.text: Indoctrination of supporter in laundry?

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
laundry is the washing

explanation.surface: How a bra comes to be brainwashed in the wash, as a jokey question.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing someone to accept beliefs by systematic pressure is a form of mind control.

clue.text: A lot of papers about large kingdom

indicators.note: about means the stack of papers goes around the size letter

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A pile of newspapers about a great kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Fight between two people owing pounds

parts.note: money owing is due
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Two people come to blows over money one owes the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal combat between exactly two parties, classically with pistols or swords.

clue.text: Admitting knight, a duke's oddly not invited

indicators.note: admitting means the jumbled letters take in the knight's letter
oddly signals the letters of the duke phrase arranged in a strange way

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A duke strangely lets in a knight, though he was not invited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a pick of odd letters, but it is the anagram signal; 'Admitting' puts N inside UASKED, the rearranged A DUKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally not asked, so not given an invitation.

clue.text: Water lily? A great many around university

indicators.note: around tells us the many go about the university letter

parts.note: lots means a great many

explanation.surface: Plenty of water lilies surround the university.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the sacred Asian water plant often loosely called a water lily, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Crime — and chap's inappropriate reaction?

parts.note: a chap is a man, here with the possessive
laughing can be the wrong response to something serious

explanation.surface: A crime, and a man laughing at it, which is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the crime word as a man's laughter, which would be an unfitting response to a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of unlawfully killing someone without intent to murder.

clue.text: Large antelope encountered in many a land

indicators.note: the letters are met with inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A big antelope that you might come across in plenty of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral-horned southern African antelope species, the male notably large and shaggy.

clue.text: First male worker, stubbornly resolute

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: The first man, a labourer, shows himself firmly determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone immovable in opinion, refusing to be persuaded.

clue.text: Large cask a crazy person brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the crazy person is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a nut is slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A huge barrel which a lunatic has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A large barrel for wine or beer, also an old measure of volume.

clue.text: A man seeks converted people similarly identified

indicators.note: converted says the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A man goes looking for converts to his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks like religious conversion of the sought people, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People who share the same name are, in effect, identified alike.

clue.text: Means to follow passenger vehicle reversing in underpass

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for means after the other piece
reversing tells us the vehicle's name is turned back to front

parts.note: a bus carries passengers
a means is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A way to tail a bus as it backs into an underpass.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a pedestrian tunnel beneath a road is called by this name, not a railway.

clue.text: Part of army ordered to seize oil installation

indicators.note: to seize means the word for ordered grabs the rig, holding it inside

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
an oil rig is a drilling installation

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told to capture an oil platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit of several battalions, a subdivision of an army.

clue.text: Touched down like some of the gentry?

definitions.meaning: an aircraft that has touched down has come to earth
the ... gentry own estates of land

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: arrived on the ground after a flight, and owning landed estates as the old gentry did.

clue.text: Conscript's simple floating structure in river

definitions.note: conscript's stands for conscript is, the 's being a link

indicators.note: in puts the raft within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a raft is a simple floating platform

explanation.surface: A conscript is like a basic raft adrift in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called up for compulsory military service, an American usage.

clue.text: Reportedly hanging about for extra allowance

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we hear the word rather than see it written

parts.note: hanging about is waiting

explanation.surface: Someone hears about loitering in return for an extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: London weighting is a British pay supplement for working in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional payment added to salary, as for living in an expensive area.

clue.text: Person who carries on war, say, for a bet?

definitions.text: Person who carries on war, say
definitions.meaning: someone who wages war, or any other campaign
a stake placed on an outcome

explanation.definitionFit: Both a punning one who wages, as in war, and a gamble staked on a result.

clue.text: Woman's anger over new drug

definitions.note: woman's stands for woman is, the 's a link

indicators.note: over puts the anger word above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: ire is anger
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman's rage at a new drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, of Greek origin meaning peace.

clue.text: Main home counties area

parts.note: the Home Counties, those surrounding London, lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: The principal region of the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as an adjective, but it is the old poetic noun for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Safe arm of the ocean

definitions.meaning: safe and ... means unharmed and in good condition
a narrow inlet or strait of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: in good, reliable condition, and a narrow sea channel such as Puget's.

clue.text: Elderly relative finally attending spectacular musical

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: Annie is the stage musical about the orphan

explanation.surface: An old relative at last goes to see a lavish stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar word for one's grandmother, typically an older family member.

clue.text: Provoke with mockery on leaving Somerset town

indicators.note: leaving says the word 'on' departs from the town's name

parts.note: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone jeers as they set off from a West Country town.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to goad or jeer at someone in order to provoke them.

clue.text: Genuine-sounding Scottish dance

indicators.note: sounding shows the word for genuine is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: An authentic-seeming dance from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish folk dance in quick time, danced in sets.

clue.text: Envy bachelor — for example, Dickens's Barnaby

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is a novel by Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: A single man is jealous of, say, the Dickens hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to resent someone else's possessions or success.
